claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and still lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. You can still qualify for Child Benefit for a child who is 16 or over, as long as they are under 20 and staying in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or an approved training course?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form doing his A-levels at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 17 and in sixth form doing A-levels, that counts as approved education.

Now I need to ask about your living situation and responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, and are you responsible for his day-to-day care?** (For example, do you provide for his food, clothes, and other needs?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives with me and I look after him. I provide everything he needs - his food, clothes, all the usual things.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work? And if so, is he working 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any paid work. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's helpful. Just a couple more questions:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. One final question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, another parent or guardian?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 17 and in approved education (sixth form doing A-levels)
✓ He lives with you and you're responsible for his care
✓ You live in the UK
✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week
✓ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
✓ Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You meet all the requirements for Child Benefit. You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex as long as he remains in approved education or training and is under 20 years old.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the online Child Benefit tax calculator to check if this applies to you.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit online or by post. If your circumstances change (for example, if Alex leaves education, starts working 24+ hours a week, or starts claiming benefits), you must inform HMRC.
